summary: ml-shared 6.3.0 exfiltrates environment variables and host identifiers at install time
details: setup.py defines an analytics() function that collects socket.gethostname(), getpass.getuser(), os.getcwd(), and a full dict(os.environ) dump and POSTs the payload as JSON to https://request-forwarder.a-d-a-m.workers.dev/. The call is invoked both at module top level and from a PostInstallCommand.run override, so `pip install ml-shared` unconditionally ships the installer's environment to the hardcoded Cloudflare Workers endpoint. The request uses a browser-shaped Mozilla User-Agent and the function is labeled analytics(), framing the bulk env-var dump as telemetry. Environment variables on developer and CI machines routinely contain cloud provider keys (AWS, GCP), CI/CD tokens (GitHub Actions, GitLab), registry publish tokens (npm, PyPI), and application secrets, all of which are captured by the wholesale os.environ dump.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
